topic: Citra Mosaic Simcoe Loral Sabro Talus Ekuanot Pahto licensed growers
finding: Yakima Chief Ranches publishes a roster of the 41 farms it works with (Washington 22, Idaho 7, Oregon 12; 43 farms in a March 2023 snapshot) and says it manages Simcoe, Citra, Mosaic and Loral through Footprints and supplies true-to-type rootstock. The roster is not broken down by variety, so no per variety licensed grower list exists on any page read. The brands page lists Ahtanum, Citra, Dolcita, Ekuanot, HBC 682, Idaho 7, Krush, Loral, Mosaic, Palisade, Sabro, Simcoe, Talus and Warrior. Yakima Chief Ranches is owned by Perrault Farms, Loftus Ranches and Carpenter Ranches. The only farm level variety data point is Simcoe at Perrault Farms in 2017 (search summary). CLS Farms and Roy Farms: CLS is not on the Yakima Chief Ranches roster and Roy Farms is; no page read states Hop Breeding Company membership for CLS, Carpenter, Perrault or Roy.

finding: The live yakimachief.com returns a bot challenge and was not worked around. Public archive copies were read instead: the October 2026 growers page lists 14 grower-owners with owner names, the April 2026 meet the growers page lists 14 including Brulotte Farms and carries the Coleman Agriculture profile, and the Yakima Chief Ranches page lists the product lines. The individual farm pages for the other 13 growers were never archived, so their founding years, acreage and varieties remain unsourced, and the Cryo processing facility location is not stated.

finding: Haas history page says the Hop Breeding Company was formed by Haas and Select Botanicals LLC; other sources say Haas and Yakima Chief Ranches. A search result summary says Select Botanicals Group reverted to the name Yakima Chief Ranches in August 2018. No farm level propagation source for Citra or Mosaic was found.

The only licensed grower named is CLS Farms (2022, Sultana, Lotus, Calypso, Altus). The announcement names no other licensed growers. No Hopsteiner farms page exists in the archive (hopsteiner.com/hop-farms, hopsteiner.us and its growers pages have no snapshot) and the grower material is behind a portal. finding: Indie Hops publishes a grower list: F & B Farms and Nursery, Fobert Farms, BC Hop Farms, B & D Hop Farms, Sodbuster Farms, Crosby Hop Farm, and Roy Farms (licensed to grow, process and sell). Goschie Farms and Coleman Agriculture are named as Indie Hops growers of multiple public varieties and are not stated to grow Strata.
CLS Farms' own site names these as its proprietary varieties. No licensed grower list for them was found.
The NASS table prints the designation VGXP01. The tie to Virgil Gamache Farms is from a search result summary only; no licensing list was found.
Gooding Farms' own site names Idaho Gem Brand 2012G01 Variety. No other grower is named.

No source gives a complete national grower list. 113 farm rows are recorded: Washington 28, Oregon 23, Idaho 17, Michigan 25, New York 12, Colorado 5, Minnesota 1, state not stated 2. Idaho is now complete against the one official list found: the 2026 Idaho State Department of Agriculture list names 17 distinct active hop growers (18 grower numbers, Gooding Farms twice) and all 17 are rows. Oregon has no official list; the Oregon Hop Commission board names 6 farms and the Yakima Chief Ranches roster adds 12, and the Oregon Encyclopedia says fewer than 30 families grow hops. Washington is the largest gap: 22 Yakima Chief Ranches roster farms plus other sourced farms against about 70 Pacific Northwest farms (trade newsletter, 2023) and no public Washington Hop Commission roster. Michigan has 25 names against more than 20 reported growers. Wisconsin (about 100 producers reported) has no named farm.

Oregon Hop Commission: the site lists the 2025 to 2026 board only (7 grower seats, 1 vacant; 6 farms named), not members. Idaho: the Idaho State Department of Agriculture publishes the full licensed grower list (read). Washington: the Washington State Hop Commission has no site of its own (wahops.org redirects to Hop Growers of America), the WSDA commission page carried no commissioner or grower names in the first 100000 characters, and the Hop Growers of America grower directory is a supplier directory. The HGA annual report and statistical packet PDFs were too large or binary to read.

New York: one farm read directly (Foothill Hops, Munnsville, in the state farm directory) plus two pelletizers from a Cornell FAQ; 11 further New York farm rows rest on search summaries. Cornell Small Farms said in 2018 that no New York grower had more than 40 acres. hopgrowersofnewyork.org redirects away and no member list was read. Wisconsin: the Wisconsin Hop Exchange grower map page returned no list; about 100 producers are reported and none are named. Vermont: no source read. California: no farm; 16 Quartz Hop Farm in the HGA directory may be Californian. The Northeast Hop Alliance and University of Vermont directories were not found in search.

Now confirmed as an active licensed Idaho grower (number 101, Boundary County) on the 2026 Idaho list. Ownership by Anheuser-Busch and a Bonners Ferry location are still only from a search summary of Edible Idaho, which could not be fetched.
